about: E12: one policy carried to five enforcers. policy-a0 (the E1 policy, sha256:ff160f6890cab76c895ec3ea3e9c7dacdf53c8340179debed60469ef12858334) translated by sharness-ai policy translate to Landlock (what ran tonight), bubblewrap, Docker, Kubernetes and the Claude Code sandbox, with the tool's own notes per target (headed "not enforced"; some lines state what the target does enforce, e.g. bwrap sets no_new_privs, and the Landlock notes are a mapping, so they are kept verbatim and not counted). Translated, not run: bwrap is not installed here, and running the Docker form would pull an image from a registry.
where: R1 Claude Code cloud, riskmandate-personal (harness.1's container; uid 0, all capabilities, no seccomp before any policy)

tool_notes: files.read, files.exec, files.write: Landlock path rules; network: an empty namespace or Landlock TCP ports; caps: rlimits and cgroups; no_new_privs: set
not yet in the CLI: per-component uids, seccomp, mutual TLS, the launcher (see sharness.ai/design/containment)
no_new_privs: bwrap sets it (PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS) for the sandboxed process
files.exec: not distinct from files.read; a read-only bind is also executable in bwrap (use noexec mounts or Landlock inside)
files.write: a writable bind is also executable in bwrap; sharness-ai run never grants execute on a writable path
process.max_memory_mb 1024: not enforced by bwrap; prefix with `prlimit --as=1073741824` or run under a cgroup
process.max_pids 16: not enforced by bwrap; `prlimit --nproc=16` or a pids cgroup

targets.form: docker run --rm --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user 65534:65534 --network none --memory 1024m --pids-limit 16 -v /opt/hx/bin:/opt/hx/bin:ro -v /opt/hx/ws:/opt/hx/ws:ro -v /opt/node22:/opt/node22:ro -v /opt/hx/ws/out:/opt/hx/ws/out python:3.12-alpine node a0-consensus.mjs
tool_notes: image python:3.12-alpine is named by tag; pin it by digest (image@sha256:…) so the policy binds to one build
files.read of system paths (/usr, /lib, /bin, /sbin, /etc): taken from the image, not bound from the host
files.exec: not distinct from read; everything readable in the image is executable (Docker has no exec allowlist)
the policy hash: Docker does not check one; the launcher's --expect-hash has no equivalent

targets.form:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: harnessed
  labels: { app: harnessed }
spec:
  automountServiceAccountToken: false
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 65534
    seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: python:3.12-alpine
      args: ["node", "a0-consensus.mjs"]
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
      resources:
          limits:
            memory: 1024Mi
      volumeMounts:
          - name: w0
            mountPath: "/opt/hx/ws/out"
  volumes:
      - name: w0
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: harnessed-egress
spec:
  podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: harnessed } }
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress: []
tool_notes: image python:3.12-alpine is named by tag; pin it by digest (image@sha256:…) so the policy binds to one build
files.read: the image's filesystem, read-only; host paths are not bound (a policy's read list becomes the image's contents)
files.exec: no execute allowlist in a securityContext
files.write: each path becomes an emptyDir volume (not the host's folder)
process.max_pids: no per-pod pids limit in the Pod spec (the kubelet's podPidsLimit is cluster-wide)
seccompProfile RuntimeDefault is the runtime's default filter, not the policy's syscall list
the policy hash: nothing in Kubernetes checks it; an admission controller could

files.read: not an allowlist in the sandbox; it reads most of the machine unless paths are listed in filesystem.denyRead (the policy's read list cannot be expressed as a deny list without knowing the machine)
files.exec: no equivalent; the sandbox has no execute allowlist
covers Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and their children only; the built-in file and web tools, hooks, MCP servers and the harness itself are outside it (per its documentation)
network none: expressed as an empty allowedDomains with strictAllowlist; the proxy refuses every host (UDP and ICMP cannot leave the sandbox per its documentation)
process.max_memory_mb / max_pids: no equivalent in the sandbox settings
the policy hash: settings are read by the agent's own process (a Setting in ABP terms); managed settings make them a Boundary for the user, not for the harness

read_across: files.exec has no equivalent outside Landlock: bwrap, Docker, Kubernetes and the Claude Code sandbox all make what is readable executable. The E1 refusal of /bin/sh (spawn-shell) is a Landlock row only.
the policy hash binds only where the launcher checks it (--expect-hash): Docker, Kubernetes and the Claude Code settings do not check one.
files.read as an allowlist exists in Landlock and bwrap (binds); Docker and Kubernetes take it from the image; the Claude Code sandbox reads most of the machine unless denied.
memory and pids: Docker and Kubernetes hold memory; pids only Docker (per pod: cluster-wide); bwrap and the Claude Code sandbox need prlimit or a cgroup.
